text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] rtv-hosted-prod: p95 latency > 1200ms, queue depth > 300 for last 5m. alert_threshold=3

alex (oncall): paging oncall. I'm taking it. looks like token service is spiking and streams are piling up. starting triage.

jess (sre): joining. can you paste the grafana dashboard? which service shows backpressure?
alex (oncall): dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/rtv/serving-overview?orgId=1 panel shows live-resp latency and grpc_tx_errors. p95 jumped at 02:07 UTC.
maria (eng-runtime): seeing a surge in open connections to the realtime muxer, kvcache hits are fine but cpu on inference nodes is high. suspect streaming session handling holding worker threads.

tyler (support): any customer-facing impact yet? support queue getting one mention from acct: AcmeCorp about 503 on streaming endpoint.

jess (sre): probability that disabling long-lived streaming will reduce socket churn and lower tail latency by reducing context-switching. propose temporary toggle: disable realtime streaming responses for hosted-api tier for 10-15m, fallback to non-streaming (polling/chunked).

alex (oncall): agreed. need to coordinate: ops flip flag, eng-runtime confirm, support message customers, monitor.
maria (eng-runtime): I have a safe admin route. command to set flag for hosted: 
```
# curl to admin service
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://admin.redwood/api/v1/feature-flags/toggle \
  -d '{"flag":"realtime_streaming","env":"hosted","enabled":false,"duration_minutes":15}'
```

jess (sre): also apply a temporary per-key rate cap increase on generation endpoints to avoid thundering herd when clients reconnect. recommend 20rps -> 10rps per key for 15m.

alex (oncall): @deploy-bot please run the flag set and apply rate-limit.
deploy-bot: acknowledged. running job #4672. will report back after both ops steps complete. :gear:

(2m) deploy-bot: feature flag update success: realtime_streaming(hosted)=false (expires in 15m). rate-limit rule updated: hosted-generation default=10rps.

maria (eng-runtime): confirmed on runtime side: stream handler closed incoming upgrade requests with 425 and sent advisory header to clients to reconnect via polling endpoint. logs: 
```
[02:10:15] INFO stream_gate: toggled off for env=hosted by admin_user
[02:10:16] WARN connection: closed stream session id=abc123 reason=feature_flag_disabled
```

jess (sre): metrics update: p95 latency dropped from 1200ms -> 420ms within 90s, queue depth down from 320->60. CPU on inference nodes reduced ~35%.

tyler (support): sending out templated note to customers on affected endpoints summarizing temporary change and mitigation steps. draft: 
"We're temporarily switching streaming responses to a polling-style response for stability. This is expected to last ~15 minutes. No persisted data lost. If you see errors, please retry with the non-streaming endpoint."

oliver (pm): keep me posted on customer escalations. prioritize AcmeCorp if they don't recover.

alex (oncall): fine to notify status page and post in #general-alerts. I'll keep the thread open and observe for collisions.
jess (sre): also refining a mitigations checklist: 1) disable streaming 2) apply per-key throttle 3) increase short-term connection limit on proxies 4) monitor for reconnect storms 5) re-enable with canary.
maria (eng-runtime): implementing step 3: bump proxy max_conn_per_ip to 8 for hosted pool. config command: 
```
kubectl apply -f proxy-config-hosted.yaml --record
# proxy-config-hosted.yaml changes: max_conn_per_ip: 8
```

alex (oncall): seeing reconnects spike briefly after flag flip but no error surge. p95 holding. good.

tyler (support): AcmeCorp reported degraded UX but no data loss. they appreciate the heads-up. leaving ticket open and tagging SRE for follow-up.

(8m) deploy-bot: rate-limit rollback job scheduled at +15m. feature flag auto-expire at +15m.

jess (sre): decision checkpoint at +12m: if p95 remains < 600ms and queue < 100, we'll roll streaming back gradually via canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%. if not, extend window and consider fallback model variants.

maria (eng-runtime): ready for canary script. quick snippet: 
```
# enable canary for 5% traffic
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://admin.redwood/api/v1/feature-flags/canary \
  -d '{"flag":"realtime_streaming","env":"hosted","canary_pct":5}'
```

alex (oncall): handing off to jess for the rest of the window, I'm going offline for a paging rotation. summary for handoff: "disabled realtime streaming for hosted, applied 10rps per-key throttle, bumped proxy conn limit. p95 down to 420ms, queue reduced. monitor for reconnect storms. support notified AcmeCorp." jess (sre): taking over. I'll keep this thread updated with the 5/10/15 minute snapshots.

(15m) jess (sre): current status: p95=390ms, queue=48, cpu nodes stable. no new customer high-severity incidents. proceeding to canary at 5%.

(20m) jess (sre): canary at 5% looks ok, p95 1% upward but within SLO. advancing to 25%.

(25m) jess (sre): 25% canary stable. starting global re-enable. will monitor for 10m.

(35m) jess (sre): global stream re-enable complete. metrics stable. closing mitigation. follow-ups: - add a circuit-breaker to stream handler to shed long-held sessions faster - add synthetic tests for streaming churn - consider making per-tenant streaming cap configurable.

alex (oncall): back from rotation. thanks team. I'll add notes to the incident log and tag postmortem if needed. :thumbsup:

tyler (support): closing customer ticket after confirmation from AcmeCorp. they are good.

deploy-bot: incident summary posted to /incidents/logs/1798801234-summary.

jess (sre): closing thread, will escalate to a postmortem if we see recurrence in next week. :white_check_mark:
